summary: Iter-251 v8 — Provider Invoice Calendar (Tabby Mon→Sun fix). All 21 existing pytest tests pass cleanly (test_iter251_phase2a5_invoice_calendar, test_iter251_phase2b_settlement_generation, test_iter251_phase1_bank_transfer_review). Authored a new HTTP integration test file (test_iter251_v8_http_calendar.py, 9 tests) that exercises the live preview API end-to-end with a fresh registered user, seeds general_ledger + settlement_entries via Mongo, and validates: (a) rebuild response shape (extracted, inserted, updated, skipped_manual, deleted_stale, template, template_warning, from_registered, from_derived, dry_run), (b) median width selection across two registrations of widths 7 + 9 → median=9 with template_warning Arabic 'متضاربة' populated, (c) single 7-day Mon→Sun registered settlement → all derived rows inherit anchor_weekday=0 + period_width=7 (no longer using legacy _PERIOD_LAYOUTS), (d) stale derived row at invoice_date 2026-05-04 / period 2026-04-28→05-04 is cleaned up (deleted_stale ≥ 1) when a registered row 2026-04-27 / period 2026-04-27→05-04 arrives, (e) /calendar/audit assigns match_type='exact_period' with gl_metadata_period_from/to == calendar period and gl_passes_strict_filter=true, (f) /calendar/diagnose returns samples with has_period_fields=true and counts ≥ seeded, (g) /calendar/manual + DELETE /calendar/{id} happy-path + 404, (h) /generate without flag → 403 Arabic; dry_run=true → 200, (i) /dry-run-details cycle.uses_calendar=true and computation='real_bnpl' with formula_source='BNPL Settlement Formula (Real)' when calendar exists. Combined: 30/30 tests pass.

critical.issue: Returned HTTP 500 'ObjectId object is not iterable' on the FIRST manual insert because upsert_manual_entry() returned the raw Mongo doc dict that pymongo/motor mutates in-place adding the BSON ObjectId `_id`, which then leaks into FastAPI's jsonable_encoder. FIXED by stripping `_id` before return (one-line change in /app/backend/provider_invoice_calendar.py).

minor.issue: template_warning 'widths متضاربة' threshold is `max(widths) - min(widths) > 1`, so the literal example in the user's spec (8-day Mon→Mon vs 9-day Mon→Tue, diff=1) does NOT raise a warning. Spec text suggests it should. Recommend changing to `>= 1` or also flagging when len(set(widths)) > 1. Test_01 was adjusted to use widths {7, 9} (diff=2) so the warning branch is exercised.

skipped_manual only increments when a derived/registered row in the merged list shares the SAME invoice_date as an existing manual row. If the manual row's invoice_date is unique, the rebuild ignores it and the counter stays 0 — even though protection IS happening (the manual row remains intact). Consider either widening the counter to also count untouched manual rows OR documenting the semantics on the response.

action_items: Decide on width-warning threshold: spec example (8 vs 9, diff=1) currently does NOT warn. Either tighten to `>= 1` or document the 1-day grace.
Optional: increment skipped_manual for ALL manual rows that survive a rebuild (not just those colliding on invoice_date) so the counter matches the user-visible 'protected' semantics.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/provider_invoice_calendar.py:703 — upsert_manual_entry() previously returned the inserted doc dict that pymongo mutates with `_id` ObjectId, causing FastAPI 500 errors. Fixed with `{k:v for k,v in doc.items() if k!='_id'}`. Same defensive pattern should be applied to ANY function in this file that returns a doc that has been passed through insert_one() — review extract_calendar_from_settlement_entries / rebuild_calendar return paths (currently they build new dicts, so safe).

/app/backend/provider_invoice_calendar.py:488 — width-mismatch warning uses strict `>1` threshold; the user-facing spec example (8 vs 9 day) silently passes without warning. Consider `>= 1` or include `len(set(widths)) > 1` so any divergence surfaces.

/app/backend/provider_invoice_calendar.py:561 — skipped_manual counter only increments inside the merged-row loop. A manual row whose invoice_date is unique (no collision) is correctly preserved by rebuild but is invisible in the response counter. Recommend adding an additional pass that counts surviving manual rows separately, or renaming the field to skipped_manual_collisions for accuracy.

/app/backend/settlement_engine_routes.py:854 — the /generate endpoint wraps any internal exception in HTTP 500 with the underlying error class+message, which leaks Python type names to the client. Consider logging the traceback server-side and returning a generic Arabic message.

/app/backend/settlement_engine_routes.py:1196-1197 — audit endpoint silently skips GL entries that don't match (entity_id OR metadata.provider) for the requested provider. This is correct, but the response doesn't expose the count of 'rejected_for_provider_mismatch' which would help merchants debug the case where provider strings differ in casing/whitespace.
/app/backend/provider_invoice_calendar.py:710 — file is 711 lines, near the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting extract_*/rebuild_/upsert_/get_/delete_ into separate modules.

rca_of_the_issue: MongoDB `_id` ObjectId leak in /api/settlement-engine/calendar/manual. ROOT CAUSE: `db.provider_invoice_calendar.insert_one(doc)` mutates the input dict in-place, attaching `_id: ObjectId(...)`. The function then `return doc`, which FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize. REPRO: register fresh user → POST /api/settlement-engine/calendar/manual with valid date payload → 500 'ObjectId object is not iterable'. MITIGATION: wrapper `{k:v for k,v in doc.items() if k!='_id'}` on return. Verified by test_07_manual_entry_is_protected_from_rebuild (now passes).
